defect_families.evidence: Every time in the new code comes from the injected Clock: the ledger claim/dispatch/completion instants, the intake processed_at, and the SmartPromptMachine cutoff. The authorization's own issue_updated_at is caller data and never becomes a cutoff, ordering or admission decision -- test_caller_supplied_issue_time_is_never_execution_authority drives a year-2099 value through a successful execution. The intake boundary's own trusted-cutoff sampling (max of clock and newest durable admission, taken after the write lock) is unchanged and still owns the authority cutoff. Naive datetimes are refused (test_ledger_rejects_naive_times).

The ledger makes no decision across two views: claim does its existence check and its insert inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and both state transitions are single conditional UPDATE statements whose WHERE clause carries the expected prior state and the exact authorization digest, so there is no read-then-write split to drift. The ADR 0036 boundary's single-snapshot authority-plus-write transaction is used unchanged. The compiler resolves authority a second time, later and outside that lock; that resolution can only observe an equal or newer authority head, so a restrictive successor blocks the build rather than being missed -- the drift direction is fail-closed, and the already-durable intake is governed by its own snapshot.

No identity in this path is caller-selected. authorization_id is recomputed from the document's claims and the carried value is only compared, never trusted (test_replay_identity_is_bound_to_exact_authorization_content). document_id comes from the existing content-derived evidence_document_id, execution_owner_id and the intake candidate_id are derived from the recomputed authorization identity, and the recorded label is the repository constant rather than the Issue's own labels. The ledger binds each row to both the identity and a digest of the complete document, so a transition cannot be applied under a different content (test_ledger_transitions_require_the_exact_claimed_content).

An unverifiable document is refused before any other decision, and a malformed or absent issuer verifying key fails bootstrap closed (test_missing_or_malformed_issuer_verifying_key_fails_closed, test_absent_issuer_verifying_key_fails_closed). The authorization parser requires the exact field set, a canonical 128-character lowercase hexadecimal signature, the exact schema version and the exact governed label, rejects duplicate JSON keys, non-integer or non-positive issue numbers, blank required fields and oversized documents. Configuration is all-or-nothing: each of the eight required variables fails closed on absence, and a malformed verification key fails closed. Absent authority is never read as permission -- an absent authority database, an unpublished document scope and an earlier cutoff all raise rather than substituting current state (test_absent_authority_database_cannot_degrade_to_a_test_double, test_missing_source_handling_authority_for_the_document_fails_closed, test_unknown_document_scope_is_returned_as_absence_not_substituted, test_authority_absent_at_an_earlier_cutoff_is_not_substituted_by_current_state).

The intake reference deliberately carries only the two governed operational metadata fields, and the labels value is the repository constant rather than the Issue's own labels, so no Issue-controlled text can ride into a durable row through the operational-metadata category (test_intake_reference_carries_only_governed_operational_metadata). Issue title and body travel only through their own governed categories, and the resolved FACT persistence restriction and POLICY retention decision block the durable write when they do not permit it (test_fact_persistence_restriction_blocks_durable_intake_and_dispatch, test_denied_retention_blocks_durable_intake_and_dispatch), with no dispatch and no durable document in either case. Downstream, the handoff is non-content lineage only (test_no_issue_text_reaches_the_fallback_runtime).

Ledger state advances only forwards: each transition names its expected prior state, so completion cannot skip the durable dispatch record and a completed authorization can be neither re-dispatched nor re-claimed (test_ledger_state_is_monotonic). Ownership survives a process restart because it is durable rather than in-memory (test_replay_after_process_restart_does_not_execute_again, test_ledger_survives_a_reopened_database), and a crash between the durable handoff record and the dispatch leaves a row that refuses the retry (test_crash_between_handoff_persistence_and_dispatch_cannot_duplicate). Every one of these runs under a frozen clock, so no ordering guarantee depends on the clock advancing.

Trusted origin is now proved rather than assumed. The workflow that observes the owner's issues:labeled event signs the exact canonical claims with a domain-separated Ed25519 issuer key, and the composition root verifies that signature against a bootstrap-captured public key before the ledger claim, durable intake or dispatch; the execution side holds only the public half, so it can verify an owner authorization and never mint one. A document with correct public claims and a correctly derived identity but no trusted proof cannot dispatch, leaves no ledger row and ingests nothing (test_valid_public_claims_without_the_trusted_issuer_proof_cannot_dispatch). A genuine signature cannot be transplanted onto different claims, and mutating any covered claim while re-deriving the digest is still refused (test_a_signature_lifted_from_another_authorization_is_refused, test_the_issuer_proof_covers_every_authorization_claim, test_issue_number_is_covered_by_the_issuer_proof). The authorization also binds the exact operation: the task key, prompt profile and route registry are repository constants and the branch, checkout and destination come from captured configuration (test_issue_text_cannot_choose_route_provider_destination_or_merge). Downstream the signed envelope remains the only accepted lineage (test_tampered_handoff_fails_the_existing_verifier, test_signing_key_swapped_after_bootstrap_cannot_issue_a_dispatchable_handoff).

This review is a fresh complete adversarial batch over the exact base->HEAD content of 3a73af22f261fa38611926d3aa996a2aecd724a3..HEAD, covering all eleven required dimensions and every applicable recurring-defect family. The previous review of this candidate was invalidated by the content mutation that repaired the blocking finding from independent owner review, so it was re-taken rather than carried forward. Three findings are recorded below: two found by the earlier pass and repaired, and F-3, the blocking finding independent review raised and this head repairs.

This is the family the blocking finding belongs to. The authorization artifact was bound to its own content by a public digest only, which makes a hand-edited document detectable but a forged one perfectly plausible, because every input to the digest is public. It is now bound by a domain-separated Ed25519 signature over the exact canonical claims, so a forged artifact is detectable rather than merely implausible (test_valid_public_claims_without_the_trusted_issuer_proof_cannot_dispatch, test_a_signature_lifted_from_another_authorization_is_refused, test_the_issuer_proof_covers_every_authorization_claim). The other repository-owned artifacts in this change keep their existing content bindings: the pre-ready review binds the base->HEAD change set excluding itself, and docs/DEFECT_REGISTRY.json is validated by the Artifact Guard.

The prior head restated caller-chosen metadata as provenance: it compared the document's own authorized_by string to configured owner text, which authenticates nothing. The proof now authenticates the writer -- only the workflow holding the issuer secret can mint a document the composition root accepts. The proof is one the authorized channel can actually produce: the workflow already observes the exact issues:labeled event, and it is given the signing secret plus a pinned cryptography install under requirements/ci-constraints.txt, so it is not handed an obligation it cannot satisfy. Absent or malformed key material fails the authorization closed rather than emitting an unsigned document (test_missing_or_malformed_issuer_signing_key_fails_closed, test_authorization_without_an_issuer_signing_authority_fails_closed), and the key is read only from machine-only configuration, never from argv (test_issuer_key_is_never_accepted_from_the_command_line).

Every commit in the governed range carries author and committer 'Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>', each resolving independently to the authorization-bound writer identity in docs/CODE_WRITE_POLICY.json; implementation-agent attribution stays in Co-Authored-By and Claude-Session trailers and never touches the identity headers. Verified on this exact head by scripts/hunter_writer_provenance.py --check-config and --check-range HEAD, and enforced again by the pre-push boundary. This change alters no part of that mechanism.

The candidate is a four-commit range published across two ordinary pushes, with no rewind, amend, rebase or force-push at any point, and none was needed to produce evidence for any commit: range-level push provenance covers the intermediate commits from the authenticated push of the exact head. The first three commits were already admitted on the previous head under exactly that rule. This change alters no part of that mechanism.

Demonstrated rather than merely asserted on this candidate: the previous head's pre-ready review was invalidated by the content mutation that repaired the blocking finding, and it was re-recorded against the new content rather than carried forward, which is what forced this fresh adversarial pass. The review artifact remains the final mutation of the candidate, binds the base->HEAD change set excluding itself, and no receipt inherited from the base branch is read as a claim about this candidate.

This change touches no admission controller, and the family's behaviour was observed live on this pull request: Hunter Governance Review published failure for an absent exact-head trusted proof at PR open, which is the specified verdict for absent rather than running evidence, then re-evaluated on the proof's workflow_run completion and published success. No head was left Ready while unadmitted, and the pending verdict was reserved for the still-running Merge Readiness gate.

findings.evidence: The first draft claimed durable ownership before performing the purely local mapping validation, so an authorization that could never execute -- an Issue with an empty body, say -- still permanently consumed its own identity. Repaired by moving the pure mapping and its validation ahead of the claim; nothing durable or external happens before the claim, so the ownership-before-execution ordering is unchanged. Pinned by test_empty_issue_body_fails_closed and test_crash_before_any_execution_still_owns_the_authorization.

Forged Issue content resolves to a governed document scope for which no FACT, POLICY or FIELD_CATEGORY_REGISTRY was ever published, so it fails closed before a build exists. Pinned by test_a_forged_authorization_still_cannot_execute_arbitrary_content. Superseded as a security argument by F-3: this gate is real but governs content classification, not who authorized execution.

Raised by independent owner review of head 3667951a. The authorization document was forgeable at the production composition boundary: its SHA-256 authorization_id covers only public Issue fields, so any caller reaching the credential-free issuer endpoint could recompute it and mint a byte-valid document, and comparing authorized_by to configured owner text compares attacker-chosen text to a constant. The earlier disposition treated this as non-blocking and delegated transport authentication to the operator while the repository-owned workflow supplied no authenticator at all, and it leaned on Source Handling as a second gate -- which governs whether an exact document scope may be processed, so for an Issue whose exact content already carries published authority it admits a forged authorization as readily as a genuine one. That disposition was wrong and this head repairs it: the workflow signs the exact canonical claims with a domain-separated Ed25519 issuer key held only as a repository secret, and the composition root verifies that signature against a public key captured once at trusted bootstrap, before the ledger claim, before durable intake and before any dispatch. Recorded as TOA-001 in docs/DEFECT_REGISTRY.json. Pinned by test_valid_public_claims_without_the_trusted_issuer_proof_cannot_dispatch and five further regressions.
